conclusions: Low-index resolution of tied visit maxima contributes to observed search8 degradation
Prior tie resolution changes selected action but does not repair visit-based training targets
Negative values with zero unvisited Q spread visits in controlled test; isolated combat FPU causality remains untested
Zero neural values have mixed results; no justification for production value removal
More simulations improve phase coverage on these recipes with higher cost; no victories
limitations: Nine shared training recipes, not eighteen independent scenarios or an independent final benchmark
Rule trajectories duplicated across model seeds
Value error is relative to a particular continuation policy
High target entropy alone is not proof of an incorrect target
next: G2.3e: versioned prior-tie and FPU/target comparisons on train/validation; freeze fresh final test before smoke and three-round learning verification
